artworks.title: Bacchus
artworks.description: Uffizi oil: the youthful wine god reclining with a shallow glass, crowned with vine leaves beside overripe fruit — Caravaggio's fleshy, faintly drowsy Bacchus as sensuality edged with decay.

artworks.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
artworks.description: National Gallery, London: Bacchus leaps from his cheetah-drawn chariot toward Ariadne on Naxos — the cycle's rescue climax, her crown already among the stars.

artworks.title: The Dionysus Cup
artworks.description: Munich kylix: Dionysus reclines in a ship whose mast sprouts grapevines, dolphins circling — the Homeric Hymn's Tyrrhenian pirates transformed, the god's voyage as black-figure miracle.

artworks.title: Bacchus
artworks.description: Bargello marble: a swaying, drunken Bacchus raising his cup while a satyr nibbles grapes behind him — intoxication carved in stone by the young Michelangelo.

music.title: L'Arianna
music.description: Monteverdi's lost Gonzaga opera survives chiefly in Ariadne's lament — the cry of the woman Bacchus will claim on Naxos, the wine god arriving as consolation after Theseus' sail.

music.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
music.description: Roussel's ballet for the Paris Opéra retells the Naxos rescue in bright neo-classical colour — Dionysus' arrival as choreography rather than Theban tragedy.

popCulture.title: The Bacchae
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' last tragedy keeps the Dionysus cycle's Theban climax on every modern stage — the god who arrives as stranger and tears the city's king apart.

popCulture.title: Dionysus
popCulture.description: Wine, theatre and ecstatic cult still orbit Dionysus' cycle — the twice-born god as Europe's name for sacred intoxication.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Dionysus' boons are hangover and festive fog — the wine god as a party build, cheering Zagreus on from Olympus between cups.
